title: First Day of Winter (Northern Hemisphere) 2026
desc: The december solstice of 2026 falls on December 21, 2026 at 20:48 UTC — the astronomical start of winter in the Northern Hemisphere (summer below the equator).

Astronomically, this is the Sun at its southernmost point — winter begins in the north, summer in the south. It is also the day the tide of daylight turns: after the December solstice the change is barely minutes per week, then accelerates — the reason the weeks after a solstice feel darker (or lighter) faster than the solstice day itself.
facts: Seasons flip in the Southern Hemisphere

title: First Day of Spring 2027
desc: The march equinox of 2027 falls on March 20, 2027 at 20:23 UTC — the astronomical start of spring in the Northern Hemisphere (autumn below the equator).

Astronomically, this is the moment the Sun crosses the celestial equator heading north — autumn in the Southern Hemisphere. It is also the day the tide of daylight turns: after the March solstice the change is barely minutes per week, then accelerates — the reason the weeks after a solstice feel darker (or lighter) faster than the solstice day itself.

title: First Day of Fall 2027
desc: The september equinox of 2027 falls on September 23, 2027 at 05:56 UTC — the astronomical start of fall in the Northern Hemisphere (spring below the equator).

Astronomically, this is the Sun crosses the equator heading south — spring in the Southern Hemisphere. It is also the day the tide of daylight turns: after the September solstice the change is barely minutes per week, then accelerates — the reason the weeks after a solstice feel darker (or lighter) faster than the solstice day itself.
